{{short description|American statistician}}
{{about|the statistician|the fictional soap-opera character|Diane Sugden|the songwriter|Every Road Leads Back to You}}
'''Diane Marie Lambert''' is an American statistician known for her work on [[zero-inflated model]]s, a method for extending [[Poisson regression]] to applications such as the statistics of [[manufacturing defect]]s in which one can expect to observe a large number of zeros.{{r|sage}}
A former Bell Labs Fellow, she is a research scientist for [[Google]], where she lists her current research areas as "[[algorithm]]s and theory, [[data mining]] and modeling, and economics and [[electronic commerce]]".{{r|goog}}

==Education and career==
Lambert earned her Ph.D. in 1978 from the [[University of Rochester]]. Her dissertation, supervised by W. Jackson Hall, was ''P-Values: Asymptotics and Robustness''.{{r|mgp}}
In the early part of her career, she worked as a faculty member at [[Carnegie Mellon University]]. As an assistant professor there, she did pioneering work on the [[confidentiality]] of statistical information.{{r|fienberg}}
She earned tenure at Carnegie Mellon, but moved to [[Bell Labs]] in 1986. At Bell Labs, she became head of statistics, and a Bell Labs Fellow. She moved again to Google in 2005.{{r|computefest|frontiers}}

==Recognition==
Lambert became a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 1991.{{r|fasa}} She is also a Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]],{{r|fims}} was executive secretary of the institute from 1990 to 1993,{{r|xsims}} and was one of the institute's Medallion Lecturers in 1995.{{r|medallion}}
